flashcards.topic: When Blockchain Is the Wrong Answer (Usually) - and When It Isn't
flashcards.q: The three properties ONLY a blockchain provides?
flashcards.a: 1) Shared write access without an operator (consensus over replicated execution). 2) Neutral deterministic execution between adversarial parties (smart contracts). 3) Independent verifiability (Merkle commitments + open replication). Everything else has cheaper substitutes.

flashcards.topic: When Blockchain Is the Wrong Answer (Usually) - and When It Isn't
flashcards.q: The decision tree questions in order?
flashcards.a: Q1: multiple distrusting writers? No -> database. Q2: acceptable operator exists? Yes -> shared DB/utility + audit logs. Q3: tamper-evidence vs operator OR neutral execution needed? No -> append-only log + external anchoring. Q4: global reach/stranger access? -> public chain; else permissioned only if funded forever.

flashcards.topic: When Blockchain Is the Wrong Answer (Usually) - and When It Isn't
flashcards.a: we.trade (bank trade finance, shut June 2022); B3i (insurance, July 2022); TradeLens (Maersk/IBM shipping, wound down late 2022-early 2023); ASX CHESS DLT replacement (cancelled Nov 2022, ~A$250M written off). Root cause: rivals won't fund shared infra; operator was trusted anyway.

flashcards.topic: When Blockchain Is the Wrong Answer (Usually) - and When It Isn't
flashcards.a: Stablecoins ~$300B market cap; GENIUS Act signed 7/18/2025 (93-day T-bill reserves, issuer no-yield rule). Tokenized treasuries $4B start-2025 -> >$10B Feb 2026; BlackRock BUIDL $2-3B; Fidelity/State Street reserve funds June 2026. JPMorgan Kinexys ~$2B/day interbank.

flashcards.topic: When Blockchain Is the Wrong Answer (Usually) - and When It Isn't
flashcards.q: Anchoring pattern - what it does and doesn't deliver?
flashcards.a: Append-only log + Merkle root published to external trust point per period: tamper-EVIDENCE against the operator at ~zero cost (RFC 6962 pattern). Does NOT deliver shared writes between distrusting parties or neutral execution - the exact boundary where blockchains begin.

flashcards.topic: When Blockchain Is the Wrong Answer (Usually) - and When It Isn't
flashcards.a: PII never on-chain; hashes of personal data are still personal data (pseudonymization != anonymization, EDPB). Crypto-shredding: encrypt off-chain, destroy keys for erasure. Design before launch - retrofitting immutability is impossible by definition.

flashcards.topic: When Blockchain Is the Wrong Answer (Usually) - and When It Isn't
flashcards.q: Cost lines blockchain adds vs a database?
flashcards.a: Latency (ms -> seconds-minutes finality), full replication per validator, governance ceremonies for changes, HSM/ceremony/recovery key management, leaky privacy layers, no DELETE. Justified only if removing the trusted operator pays for all of it annually, forever.

flashcards.topic: When Blockchain Is the Wrong Answer (Usually) - and When It Isn't
flashcards.a: Bounded identified membership; validator funding committed long-term; confidentiality beyond public+ZK today; regulatory constraints on public settlement. Kinexys qualifies. Missing any -> public L1/L2 with compliance wrappers or no chain at all.

flashcards.topic: When Blockchain Is the Wrong Answer (Usually) - and When It Isn't
flashcards.q: Compliance stack on public chains - components?
flashcards.a: Allowlisted wallets via transfer-restriction code in tokens, KYC at custody/on-ramp boundaries, continuous sanctions screening, travel-rule messaging, freeze/pause/recover roles for regulators/courts, chain-analytics surveillance. Every control re-centralizes a slice - that's the honest tradeoff.

flashcards.topic: When Blockchain Is the Wrong Answer (Usually) - and When It Isn't
flashcards.a: Federal payment-stablecoin framework (signed 7/18/2025): 93-day T-bill/deposit/MMF reserves, monthly disclosure, licensing pathways, no-yield-to-holders rule. Issuance became a compliance product decision; yield migrated to tokenized treasuries ($4B->$10B+ in 13 months). Final rules still in comment processes mid-2026.
